records.name: Desert Cottontail
records.fact: Desert cottontails get nearly all their water from the plants they eat.

requirements.hint: Brush for cover and a burrow bank to shelter in.

records.name: Kit Fox
records.preferredHabitat: A thriving desert full of prey
records.fact: Kit foxes rarely drink water at all, surviving almost entirely on moisture from prey.

requirements.hint: Kit foxes return when prey is plentiful and dens are ready.

records.name: Coyote
records.preferredHabitat: Open desert with prey and cover
records.fact: Coyote pairs duet at dusk; two voices echoing can sound like a whole chorus.

requirements.hint: Cover, shade, and prey on the move.

records.name: Kangaroo Rat
records.fact: Kangaroo rats never need to drink — their bodies make water from dry seeds.

requirements.hint: Burrow banks and seed plants nearby.

records.name: Black-tailed Jackrabbit
records.fact: A jackrabbit's enormous ears act like radiators, releasing heat to keep it cool.

requirements.hint: Open running room with brush for shade.

records.name: Greater Roadrunner
records.shelter: Low nests in brush and cactus
records.preferredHabitat: Open hunting ground with brushy edges
records.fact: Roadrunners can sprint over 20 mph and will even take on rattlesnakes.

requirements.hint: Open desert, brush, and reptile prey about.

records.name: Burrowing Owl
records.preferredHabitat: Burrow mounds with open hunting space
records.fact: Burrowing owls imitate a rattlesnake's rattle to scare intruders away from their burrows.

requirements.hint: Ready-made burrows and open ground to hunt over.

records.name: Gambel's Quail
records.fact: Quail coveys post a lookout on a high branch while the rest of the family feeds.

requirements.hint: Thick brush to hide a whole covey.

records.name: Desert Tortoise
records.preferredHabitat: Native plants with shade and burrow ground
records.fact: Desert tortoises can live 80 years, spending 95% of that time underground.

requirements.hint: Shade, native plants, and burrow habitat.

records.name: Horned Lizard
records.preferredHabitat: Sunny open ground near ant trails
records.fact: Horned lizards can squirt blood from their eyes to startle predators.

requirements.hint: Sunny rocks and sandy ground bring the ants — and the lizards.

records.name: Collared Lizard
records.fact: Collared lizards sprint on their hind legs like tiny dinosaurs.

requirements.hint: Plenty of warm rock to perch and hunt from.

records.name: Western Rattlesnake
records.preferredHabitat: Rocky shelter near busy rodent trails
records.fact: A rattlesnake adds a new rattle segment each time it sheds — but segments break, so you can't count age.

requirements.hint: Rocky shelter and rodents to hunt.

records.name: Desert Tarantula
records.fact: Desert tarantulas may live 25 years, most of it within a few feet of one burrow.

requirements.hint: Quiet, diggable ground.

records.name: Desert Scorpion
records.preferredHabitat: Rocky cover with night hunting ground
records.fact: Scorpions glow blue-green under ultraviolet light — no one is entirely sure why.

requirements.hint: Rocks to hide beneath by day.

records.name: Desert Bee
records.fact: Most desert bees are solitary — a single mother bee digs and stocks her own tiny nest.

requirements.hint: Cactus blooms are the desert's flower patch.

records.name: Mountain Goat
records.fact: Mountain goats' cloven hooves have rubbery pads that grip rock like climbing shoes.

requirements.hint: Rocky terrain and restored alpine vegetation.

records.name: Bighorn Sheep
records.fact: A bighorn ram's curled horns can weigh more than all the bones in its body combined.

requirements.hint: Grassy slopes with rocky escape ground.

records.name: American Pika
records.diet: Grasses and wildflowers, dried into haypiles
records.shelter: Cool gaps deep in talus rock
records.fact: Pikas spend all summer harvesting and sun-drying little haystacks to eat under the winter snow.

requirements.hint: Cool rock piles and flowers to harvest.

records.name: Yellow-bellied Marmot
records.fact: Marmots hibernate up to eight months a year — more than half their lives are spent asleep.

requirements.hint: Burrows, meadow patches, and open space.

records.name: Snowshoe Hare
records.fact: Snowshoe hares change coat color with the seasons — brown in summer, white in winter.

requirements.hint: Cover and forage at the treeline.

records.name: Elk
records.fact: Elk migrate up and down mountains with the seasons, following the 'green wave' of new growth.

requirements.hint: High meadow forage and snowmelt water.

records.name: Mule Deer
records.fact: Mule deer summer high in the mountains and walk the same routes back down each fall.

requirements.hint: Forage and clean water up high.

records.name: Red Fox
records.fact: Mountain foxes listen for animals moving beneath deep snow, then dive in headfirst.

requirements.hint: Foxes follow the pikas and marmots.

records.name: Pine Marten
records.fact: Pine martens hunt beneath the snowpack in winter, using tunnels no one else can reach.

requirements.hint: Rocky cover and prey near the treeline.

records.name: White-tailed Ptarmigan
records.preferredHabitat: Low shrubs and safe nesting cover
records.fact: Ptarmigan grow feathered snowshoes on their feet each winter.

requirements.hint: Alpine shrubs and quiet nesting cover.

records.name: Clark's Nutcracker
records.diet: Pine seeds, cached by the thousand
records.fact: A Clark's nutcracker can remember thousands of seed cache locations months later, even under snow.

requirements.hint: A recovering treeline with seeds to cache.

records.name: Golden Eagle
records.preferredHabitat: High, healthy country with abundant prey
records.fact: Golden eagles can spot a hare from more than a mile away and dive at over 150 mph.

requirements.hint: Eagles arrive last — when the high country is truly alive again.

records.name: Alpine Butterfly
records.fact: Some alpine butterflies take two full summers to grow up, pausing each winter under the snow.

requirements.hint: Alpine flowers in bloom.

records.name: Alpine Bumblebee
records.fact: Bumblebees shiver their flight muscles to warm up, letting them fly in near-freezing air.

requirements.hint: More flowers, more bees — even up here.

records.name: Cutthroat Trout
records.fact: Cutthroat trout need water so cold and clean that their presence is itself a health report for the mountain.

requirements.hint: Cold, clean, connected snowmelt pools.

records.name: Shore Crab
records.fact: Shore crabs can change color slowly to match their home pool.

requirements.hint: Restore the tidepools and the crabs scuttle back first.

records.name: Hermit Crab
records.fact: When a perfect shell appears, hermit crabs line up by size and swap shells in a chain.

requirements.hint: Tidepools plus washed-up shells to move into.

records.name: Ochre Sea Star
records.fact: Sea stars are keystone predators — one species' presence reshapes the whole shoreline community.

requirements.hint: Sea stars need established pools with mussels to eat.

records.name: Giant Green Anemone
records.diet: Small animals caught by stinging tentacles
records.fact: The green color comes partly from algae living inside the anemone's tissues — roommates that pay rent in sugar.

requirements.hint: Clear, quiet pools.

records.name: California Mussel
records.fact: A single mussel filters and cleans several liters of seawater every hour.

requirements.hint: Clean water over rocky shore.

records.name: Pacific Littleneck Clam
records.fact: You can estimate a clam's age by counting the growth rings on its shell, like a tree.

requirements.hint: Stable, quiet sand to dig into.

records.name: Snowy Plover
records.preferredHabitat: Protected dunes with quiet nesting beach
records.fact: Snowy plover chicks can run and feed themselves within hours of hatching.

requirements.hint: Anchored dunes and a protected stretch of quiet beach.

records.name: Western Gull
records.diet: Fish, shellfish, and whatever washes up
records.fact: Gulls drop clams onto rocks from the air to crack them open.

requirements.hint: Gulls show up as soon as there's a beach worth patrolling.

records.name: Brown Pelican
records.shelter: Quiet roosts on rocks and sand
records.fact: Brown pelicans dive from 30 feet up, with air sacs under the skin to cushion the splash.

requirements.hint: Quiet roosting space and fishable water.

records.name: Pelagic Cormorant
records.fact: Cormorant feathers soak through on purpose — less buoyancy makes them better divers.

requirements.hint: Healthy rocky shallows to dive in.

records.name: Green Sea Turtle
records.shelter: Offshore waters; nests on quiet sand
records.fact: Green sea turtles return to nest on the very beach where they hatched, decades later.

requirements.hint: An undisturbed nesting beach and clean water.

records.name: Harbor Seal
records.preferredHabitat: Calm, clean water with undisturbed shore
records.fact: Harbor seals can sleep underwater, surfacing to breathe without fully waking.

requirements.hint: Quiet beaches and clean water — seals need calm above all.

records.name: Sea Otter
records.fact: Sea otters wrap themselves in kelp before sleeping so they don't drift away — and sometimes hold hands.

requirements.hint: Kelp habitat and shellfish beds first; otters follow.

records.name: Bottlenose Dolphin
records.fact: Dolphins call each other by name, using signature whistles unique to each individual.

requirements.hint: A clean, busy shoreline brings dolphins close in.

records.name: Gray Whale
records.diet: Tiny crustaceans sifted from the seafloor
records.shelter: Open ocean; passes close to healthy shores
records.preferredHabitat: Seen offshore from a fully restored coast
records.fact: Gray whales make one of the longest migrations of any mammal — up to 14,000 miles round trip.

requirements.hint: Only a truly thriving shore earns a whale sighting. Watch the horizon.
